does: Fries soft vegetables, whole or in thick pieces, in a layer of hot oil that comes part way up their sides, turning them until they are soft right to the middle and golden all over, then drains them on paper.

intro.what: Shallow-frying vegetables cooks whole or thick pieces in a layer of hot oil, turned on every side.
intro.why: It teaches you to balance colour on the outside with softness in the middle.

how: Dry the vegetables well. Wet ones spit and do not colour.
Heat oil in a wide pan to come about a third of the way up the pieces, until a piece dropped in sizzles at once.
Lay the pieces in with room between them.
Turn them as each side goes golden, until every side is coloured and a knife meets no resistance.
Lift them out onto paper to drain.

cues.text: A lively sizzle as each piece goes in.
The piece is soft and gives all the way through when it is pressed with a spoon.
Golden on every side, with the oil still clear.

mistakes.mistake: Frying in oil that is not hot, so that the vegetable drinks the oil and turns greasy.
mistakes.fix: Wait until a test piece sizzles at once.

mistakes.mistake: Taking the pieces out when they are coloured but still firm in the middle.
mistakes.fix: Turn the heat down a little and keep turning until they are soft through.

quiz.question: Why must the oil be hot before the vegetables go in?
choices: So they colour and seal instead of drinking oil.
quiz.because: In oil that is not hot enough, soft vegetables soak it up and turn greasy.

quiz.question: How deep should the oil be?
choices: Part way up the sides of the pieces.
quiz.because: Shallow-frying uses a layer that reaches part way up, and the pieces are turned.

quiz.question: When is a piece ready?
choices: When it is golden all over and soft to the middle.
quiz.because: Both colour and softness right through are needed.

quiz.question: The pieces are golden but hard in the middle. What should change?
choices: Lower the heat a little and keep turning them.
quiz.because: A gentler heat gives the middle time to soften before the outside darkens.

variant_of.differs: Soft vegetables, whole or in thick pieces, lie in a deeper layer of oil and are turned on every side until soft right to the middle, then drained on paper.
